BOND¶

BOND (Bed of Nails Design) is Sistemi’s open source PCBA tester. It is a Teensy 4.1 based jig controller with four headers of configurable analog and digital pins, a DUT power supply, a battery emulator, and pass/fail LEDs. You design a Pogo board, with the spring probes for your DUT, that plugs into the BOND headers.

  • Product brief: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/a4402-SPC_ProductBrief_01.pdf

  • Schematic: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/a4402-SCH_05.pdf

  • Driver developer guide: public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/README.md

  • Example scripts and test code: public/prism/scripts/example/BOND_v0

Getting Started¶

  1. Program the BOND firmware into a new BOND, with the example script bond_progfresh_0.scr, or with the Arduino IDE, see public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/server/README.md. Only one BOND may be plugged in while programming.

  2. With no Pogo board or DUT connected, run the self test script bond_selftest_0.scr. It checks the BOND supplies, the header ADCs against the 2.5V reference, the battery emulator and the DUT supply.

  3. Copy the example folder to your product, for example public/prism/scripts/myproduct/BLT, and change the scripts and test code, see the example’s README.md. The P1000-P1999 test items are examples, add your own tests after them.

bond_update_0.scr updates the firmware of a BOND that is already programmed. Run it only once per Prism start, as the BOND’s USB port can change after the update. The Arduino IDE must be closed while Prism uses BOND.

Header Definition File¶

Each Pogo board has a header definition file, which sets how each header pin is used: ADC, DAC, GPO, GPI or not used. The file is given with the driver in the script config,

"config": {
  "fail_fast": true,
  "drivers": [["public.prism.drivers.A4401_BOND.hwdrv_A4401_BOND",
               "public/prism/scripts/myproduct/BLT/assets/pogo_hdr_definition._json"]]
},

  • Start from the example assets/pogo_hdr_definition._json, and use the BOND schematic Header # pages to map your Pogo board’s signals to header pins.

  • Each pin is {“mode”: <mode>, “port”: <port>}. A pin wired to two ports lists both, for example {“mode”: “ADC,GPO”, “port”: “6,9”}.

  • ADC and DAC ranges are 0-10000 mV. Each header has one GPO high level (gpo_mv) and one GPI threshold (gpi_mv).

  • HDR1 pin 1 is an adjustable LDO output (600-3900 mV), set with bond_ldo_set.

  • The file is checked when the driver loads, an invalid file fails the script Validate.

  • Different DUTs use different Pogo boards, each with its own file.

The full rules are in the driver README.md, section BOND Header Pin Configuration.

To plan which DUT test points go to which header pins, and the Pogo board circuits, see Pin Budget in PCBA Test Coverage.

Test Code¶

The setup item gets the BOND for its channel from the drivers, and records BOND’s id for traceability, see Traceability,

drivers = self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type=DRIVER_TYPE)
driver = drivers[0]
_, _, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("teensy4_id", driver["obj"]["unique_id"],
                                       ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING)
self.teensy = driver["obj"]["hwdrv"]

Each BOND method returns a dict, {‘success’: True, ‘method’: …, ‘result’: {…}}. Check success before using result,

response = self.teensy.bond_max_hdr_adc(hdr=1, pin=9)
if not response['success']:
    self.item_end(ResultAPI.RECORD_RESULT_INTERNAL_ERROR)
    return
success, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("v3v3", response['result']['mV'],
                                                   ResultAPI.UNIT_MILLIVOLTS,
                                                   ctx.item.args.min, ctx.item.args.max)

The main methods, see A4401_BOND.py for all of them and their arguments,

  • header pins: bond_max_hdr_adc, bond_max_hdr_dac, bond_max_hdr_gpo, bond_max_hdr_gpi

  • DUT supply: vdut_set, vdut_en, vdut_con, vdut_read, vdut_get_fault

  • battery emulator: vbat_set, vbat_read, iox_vbat_en, iox_vbat_con

  • other: bond_ldo_set, vbus_en, led, version, unique_id, temperature, reset

BOND is reset at the start and end of every test, which sets the DACs to 0V and the GPOs to their idle level. The BOND driver also gives Prism the jig closed detect (play) and the pass/fail LEDs (show_pass_fail), see Drivers.

Command Line¶

A4401_BOND_cli.py runs BOND methods without Prism, for bringing up a Pogo board and debugging,

cd ~/git/scripts/public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND
python A4401_BOND_cli.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 status
python A4401_BOND_cli.py -p /dev/ttyACM0 -n bond_max_hdr_adc_cal --header 3
python A4401_BOND_cli.py --help

Stop Prism, or close the script in Prism, before using the CLI, only one program can use the BOND serial port at a time.
